subject: Hospitality
title: LEED Certified Hotels
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on LEED Certified Hotels.

hook.text: LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) certification is the gold standard for green buildings.

buildup.text: LEED evaluates energy use, water efficiency, materials, indoor air quality, and innovation.

discovery.text: LEED-certified hotels use 25% less energy and 11% less water than conventional hotels. Savings compound over decades of operation.

twist.text: LEED certification doesn't guarantee lower operating costs initially. Green construction can cost 2–5% more upfront.

climax.text: LEED Certified Hotels matters because clearer reasoning leads to better judgments.

punchline.text: 25% less energy, 11% less water. Green hotels save money and the planet.

quiz.question: How much less energy do LEED-certified hotels typically use?
